scenarioStory.history: Patient was eating a steak dinner with a coworker when he suddenly stood up, grabbed his throat, and could not speak or cough. He collapsed within about a minute. The coworker attempted abdominal thrusts without success before the patient became unresponsive and stopped breathing; 911 was called immediately.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 58-year-old male supine and unresponsive on the restaurant floor following a witnessed choking event. He is apneic with no palpable pulse and visible food debris at the mouth. → CPR started, airway obstruction cleared: Crew initiates immediate high-quality chest compressions while simultaneously managing the obstructed airway: direct laryngoscopy visualizes the food bolus, which is suctioned/cleared, allowing effective two-person BVM ventilation with continuous waveform capnography in place. → ROSC achieved after airway cleared: Following successful clearance of the airway obstruction and effective CPR, the patient achieves return of spontaneous circulation. Crew transitions to post-ROSC care, securing the airway, avoiding hyperventilation, and closely monitoring for re-arrest.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Unresponsive, witnessed choking during a meal

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 58-year-old male supine and unresponsive on the restaurant floor following a witnessed choking event. He is apneic with no palpable pulse and visible food debris at the mouth.

scenarioEvents.name: CPR started, airway obstruction cleared
scenarioEvents.description: Crew initiates immediate high-quality chest compressions while simultaneously managing the obstructed airway: direct laryngoscopy visualizes the food bolus, which is suctioned/cleared, allowing effective two-person BVM ventilation with continuous waveform capnography in place.
relatedChecklist: Begin immediate high-quality chest compressions, minimally interrupted
Perform direct laryngoscopy to visualize the oropharynx; suction and clear the obstructing food bolus (SALAD technique)
Provide two-person, two-thumbs-up BVM ventilation once the airway is cleared, with PEEP
Apply continuous waveform capnography to monitor CPR quality and detect ROSC

scenarioEvents.name: ROSC achieved after airway cleared
scenarioEvents.description: Following successful clearance of the airway obstruction and effective CPR, the patient achieves return of spontaneous circulation. Crew transitions to post-ROSC care, securing the airway, avoiding hyperventilation, and closely monitoring for re-arrest.
relatedChecklist: Secure the airway and support ventilation, avoiding hyperoxygenation (target SpO2 94-98%)
Ventilate at 8-10 breaths/minute, targeting EtCO2 35-45 mmHg; avoid hyperventilation
Monitor closely for recurrence of cardiac arrest using cardiac and EtCO2 monitoring and signs of perfusion

scenarioEvents.name: Airway obstruction not cleared
scenarioEvents.description: Crew attempts bag-valve-mask ventilation without first visualizing and clearing the obstructing food bolus. No chest rise is achieved despite repeated ventilation attempts, and the patient's rhythm deteriorates toward asystole as hypoxia persists.
relatedChecklist: Recognize failed ventilation (no chest rise); reassess airway, perform direct laryngoscopy and suction to clear obstruction
